audit_findings.title: The capital bridge predates the completed $1.2 billion Riverpoint acquisition
audit_findings.magnitude: $584.0 million implied cash use ($1.2 billion less $616.0 million of borrowings), equal to $13.04/share and 28.7% of the $2.038 billion base equity value; gross debt rose to $854.8 million; an additional $250.0 million milestone is payable
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds pre-close cash that was subsequently spent, while the equity-level OE forecast lacks the new acquisition-financing interest burden.
audit_findings.evidence: Our primary ongoing cash requirements are funding operations, capital expenditures, investments in businesses, and repayment of debt and related interest payments.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch: the September 6 valuation uses a July 3 bridge even though Riverpoint closed July 23, and the filing specifies how the purchase was funded. The stale cash addition and absent financing cost materially overstate the as-filed value. Riverpoint earnings could offset that overstatement, but their amount is unresolved because purchase accounting and target operating results are unavailable.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild the bridge from a post-July 23 balance sheet, including cash consumed, $854.8 million gross debt, transaction costs, working-capital adjustments and the $250.0 million milestone; then rerun OE with Riverpoint earnings and normalized financing interest.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 reflects only a fraction of the TEU notes' recurring interest burden
audit_findings.magnitude: $11.5 million total future interest, including $6.0 million within twelve months, versus $0.9 million in FY2025; the undiscounted $11.5 million gross upper bound is $0.26/share, or 0.6% of the $45.50 base value
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-level OE retains interest expense, so growing the FY2025 anchor carries only the partial-year TEU interest burden into the forecast.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, future interest payments under the Amortizing Notes are estimated to be approximately $11.5 million through maturity based on the current contractual term, with $6.0 million payable within the next twelve months.
audit_findings.explanation: The partial-year treatment is a demonstrated timing error if no separate schedule was used. It cannot change the valuation conclusion: even treating all filed future TEU interest as completely omitted produces an undiscounted upper bound of only $0.26 per share, and the actual effect is smaller because the anchor already contains $0.9 million and the notes mature in 2028.
audit_findings.action: Replace the mechanically grown FY2025 TEU interest amount with the contractual 2026-2028 interest schedule and confirm that no note principal is deducted from OE.

audit_findings.title: Recurring restructuring and acquisition costs may have been stripped from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the $22.652 million FY2025 line equals 24.1% of the $93.9 million anchor and comprises $16.124 million of net restructuring charges and $6.528 million of acquisition and related charges
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding recurring restructuring, integration or acquisition costs back to earnings raises the OE anchor and every forecast cash flow derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: We have undertaken restructuring and realignment activities in the past, and we will continue to assess our operating and cost structure in the future.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate recurring programs and costs, including another $15.104 million during the first half of 2026, but the supplied record does not show the OE adjustment ledger. Therefore, recurrence is demonstrated while the alleged add-back remains an unresolved possibility. The exposed line is large enough to matter if it was removed wholesale.
audit_findings.action: Produce the FY2025 OE adjustment ledger by component and rerun the valuation retaining recurring acquisition, integration, severance and manufacturing-realignment costs; add back only independently supported nonrecurring items.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may under-reserve the disclosed increase in capital spending
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified sustaining portion; the latest forecast is $30-$40 million versus $15.627 million in FY2025, an increase of $14.373-$24.373 million or 15.3%-26.0% of the $93.9 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Any sustaining capital expenditure above the amount embedded in the anchor reduces forecast OE and its terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect to use approximately $20 million to $25 million in 2026 for capital expenditures related to investments in new property, plant and equipment for our existing businesses.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing increases the earlier $20-$25 million estimate to $30-$40 million and says it includes a significant China capacity expansion. The total increase is potentially material, but the record does not separate maintenance spending from discretionary capacity growth, so it does not establish the required OE reduction.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the project-level 2026 capital budget, classify maintenance, replacement, compliance and growth capacity spending, and rerun OE using the sustaining portion rather than FY2025 capital expenditures mechanically.

audit_findings.title: Keonn contingent consideration is an unbridged claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.261 million remaining fair-value liability, equal to $0.03/share and 0.06% of base equity value; even the original $21.9 million maximum equals only $0.49/share and 1.1% of base value
audit_findings.mechanism: Unpaid contingent consideration is a cash claim that should reduce bridge cash unless its settlement is already included in forecast OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Contingent consideration represents additional payments that the Company may be required to make in the future, between € 0 and € 20.0 million (approximately $ 21.9 million as of the acquisition date), depending on the achievement of specified revenue targets by Keonn during fiscal years 2025 through 2027, as well as maintaining certain minimum gross margin targets during the applicable periods.
audit_findings.explanation: The claim exists, but the latest filing shows that $4.393 million was already paid before the July 3 cash balance and only $1.261 million remained at fair value. Deducting that balance cannot change the valuation conclusion; even the original maximum payout is only 1.1% of base value.
audit_findings.action: Deduct the latest unpaid fair-value liability from the bridge or document its inclusion in forecast cash flows, and update the reserve after each remaining Keonn measurement date.

audit_findings.title: A one-off facility-sale gain may inflate the FY2025 anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.6 million, equal to 3.8% of the $93.9 million anchor; a full pre-tax removal has an upper-bound base-value effect of approximately $1.13/share, or 2.5%
audit_findings.mechanism: Retaining the nonrecurring gain raises FY2025 OE and propagates it through forecast growth and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: In January 2025, the Company sold a facility from the 2020 restructuring program and recorded a $ 3.6 million gain in the Company’s Automation Enabling Technologies segment.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the gain remains in OE is unresolved because the adjustment ledger was not supplied. Nevertheless, the entire filed gain produces only an approximately $1.13-per-share upper-bound effect under the base DCF scaling, far below the $102.86 gap between the $45.50 base value and $148.36 market price.
audit_findings.action: Verify that the $3.6 million gain was removed separately from FY2025 OE; if it was retained, remove it and rerun without adding back recurring restructuring or acquisition costs.
